o1.biggest_strength: Takes the 4.0 apart against the 2.5 break-even and puts the feed fix first, with the customer's own words in the titles.
o1.biggest_mistake: Its projection table quietly assumes brand search jumps to about 25 ROAS and PMax recovers to 2.6, which flatters the base case and undercuts the 'judge by profit' message.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the expected profit range from cautious to base with the assumptions on one line each, so the owner can see the upside is not guaranteed.

o2.biggest_strength: Uses only the owner's own numbers, gives a profit range instead of a single promise, and adds stop rules that protect the brand if the switch goes wrong.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 106-character title exceeds Google's 150 limit only in theory, but its length and order bury the searched words late and read more like keyword stuffing than the warm brand voice.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the title to the searched words first in the brand's warm, plain voice, and keep the A/B test rule.

reason: Output 2 builds every number from the owner's data, gives a profit range with stop rules, and never over-promises; Output 1's base case quietly assumes a brand ROAS of 25 that the owner did not give it.
